title: Chicago studies and the Club Lyri with Louis Tio conducting
summary: He studied at Marquette, Kimball Hall and the YMCA college, and learned conducting from Louis Tio in the nonprofit Club Lyri orchestra.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, I had, I had two years at Marquette where I had a course in public school music. And then I stood at Kimball Hall with Professor Manley, and I took my teacher's course on violin. Yeah. And I had a course of philosophy with Dr. Balduff at the Central YMCA College. Yes.
Now this is a conducting course under Lorenzo Teo.

Yes, that's, we had in those days an organization known as the Club Lyri. That was composed of a symphonic orchestra. People who played just for the love of music. It was a non-profit organization. Their sole purpose was to sponsor talented young people. We used to give two concerts a year, and whenever we found a talented person, we would sponsor them. We sent, I remember we sent one boy to Europe, pianist. And, I don't know, we've never found out what really happened. He died the week that he was to graduate, after spending almost four years in Europe. Then we sent a young violinist there by the name of Edmund Dede. And he never came back to America until he was an old man. And he died of a cancer.
mouth. But that was organization, it's through that organization I got my first training is conducting under Louie Teo. Is it Louie or Lorenzo? Louie. Louie. Yes.
Did he have regular classes at that time for it, or just take you as a private student?
You mean... Conducting. Oh yes, he did his private work, but this was something that he was interested in, and we used to meet once every week.
Who conducted the orchestra, the lyre? This one, the orchestra I'm speaking of?

Louie. Louie Teo. He was the conductor? Oh yeah, Louie Teo. He was the conductor. Yeah. At that time, I sort of... And when he found out that I was interested in that, then he used to let me take some of the smaller things that he felt I could handle. Do you remember? Louie Teo. And I became deeply interested in that phase of it, then I thought I'd study.
